commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
fix: preserve resolved PII decisions and enforce output limits (#50)

Preserve resolved PII decisions when applying REDACT or BLOCK to JSON values, including merged fallback types outside the detection allowlist. Use batch results directly so enforcement does not depend on session cache retention.

Enforce output length limits on unchanged BLOCK responses, including whitespace and original JSON formatting. Report processing-limit failures with the calling boundary's phase.

Simplify internal JSON transformation, configuration-source collection, and authorization session handling. Document that tool disclosure permissions are checked against the final entity type after merging.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
fix: scope privacy processing to runtime values (#49)

Limit privacy analysis to runtime message content, tool arguments and results, and model output. Tool descriptions, input schemas, output-format instructions, and structured-output schemas no longer trigger PII-based rejection. Tool-call structure and registered tool names remain validated.

Preserve JSON property names and value-tree map keys while protecting string and numeric values. Keys still count toward processing limits. Duplicate JSON properties are preserved in order, with each member value subject to privacy processing.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
feat: reuse PII analysis within privacy sessions (#48)

Cache successful analysis and completed tokenizations so repeated model, JSON, and tool processing can reuse results for identical text. Bound retained data, clear it on session close, and retry analysis after provider failures.

Use session-aware batching for JSON scalars and plain decimal text for BigDecimal analysis. Count newly produced raw spans across batches without recounting reused results.

Stop scanning tool names for PII while retaining structural and registered-name checks.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
feat: make privacy processing limits configurable (#47)

Replace fixed processing limits with configurable PrivacyProcessingLimits for each service, keeping the existing defaults. Apply these limits across analyzers, text and value-tree transformations, and structured JSON processing, including batch analysis and combined analyzer results.

Add Spring Boot settings for processing limits and Presidio response depth.

Custom PiiAnalyzer implementations now receive PrivacyProcessingLimits. The previous fixed processing-limit constants are removed.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
refactor: extract shared model request boundary (#46)

Extract a shared model-request boundary that runs configured privacy, tool authorization, and inspection stages in a fixed order before each model call, including tool-loop re-entry.

Move the privacy processing performed before model calls and the tool-definition authorization logic into dedicated request stages. Move Spring Boot-independent client configuration types into their runtime integration modules while keeping protection scoped to selected ChatClients.

Validate duplicate boundaries and unsupported Tool Advisor placement, and require explicit opt-in for advisors after an inspection boundary. Prepare the common request path for the content inspection work tracked in #42.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
feat: prepare privacy boundaries from available beans (#43)

Configure privacy and tool authorization from available analyzers, services, and tool policies. Allow applications without the required beans to start without creating the corresponding client configurer or factory.

Remove `spring.ai.privacy.enabled` and `spring.ai.privacy.security.enabled`. Setting these properties to `false` no longer disables the corresponding auto-configuration. Keep protection explicitly selected per `ChatClient`, while preserving analyzer-specific flags and `spring.ai.privacy.output.enabled`.

Respect injection candidate settings and scoped proxies when detecting tool policies. Resolve eligible policies and default tool managers from parent contexts. Continue requiring an explicit `SpringSecurityToolBoundary` for custom tool managers.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
feat: scope tool authorization to clients and align privacy advisors (#41)

Scope tool authorization to selected ChatClients so protected and ordinary clients can share a model without replacing its ToolCallingManager.

Replace the authorization configurers with client factories that copy tool advisor builders, including Tool Search builders, and configure the copies with the authorization-aware manager. Preserve Spring AI's automatic advisor registration and conversation history adjustment based on memory advisor placement.

Filter unauthorized tool definitions before each model call and preserve authorization checks immediately before tool execution. Position privacy advisors around the configured tool advisor order without changing application advisor orders. Account for the output protection setting when determining the allowed order range.

Validate call and stream advisor chains, including advisors added to individual requests. Require automatic registration for requests with tools and reject separately registered or PriorityOrdered tool advisors.

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
feat: add optional Spring Security tool authorization (#39)

Add optional Spring Security tool authorization with standalone and privacy-integrated configuration.

Filter unauthorized tool definitions and recheck authorization immediately before tool execution. When combined with privacy protection, authorize execution before restoring original PII.

Support Tool Search and request-scoped authorization across supported asynchronous paths. Add compatibility and publication checks for the new modules.

Closes #33

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>

commits.author: Taewoong Kim
commits.message:
fix: preserve scalar isolation in structured JSON analysis (#38)

Replace concatenated JSON scalar batches with segment-aware analysis that keeps property names, string values, and numeric values independent.

Add a compatibility-preserving `PiiAnalyzer.analyzeSegments(...)` contract and expose it through `PrivacyService`. Provide optimized segmented implementations for Presidio and OpenNLP while preserving input order, text-relative offsets, processing limits, and aggregate result limits.

Add regression coverage across the core, built-in analyzers, and Spring AI model-input and tool-input boundaries.

Closes #34

Signed-off-by: Taewoong Kim <ktw2172@gmail.com>
